stories.headline: Iran says US deal requires Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, raising prospect deal could collapse

key_facts.fact: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tuesday the tentative US-Iran deal to end the war requires Israel to withdraw from Lebanon — a condition Israel has already rejected.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Without the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the territories they occupied during this war, the war has not fully come to an end,' Araghchi said.

key_facts.fact: A US official said the deal does not call for an Israeli withdrawal; PM Netanyahu said Israel will remain in Lebanon 'as long as necessary'.
key_facts.excerpt: A U.S. official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss outlines of the agreement, has said the deal did not call for an Israeli withdrawal. And Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Monday that Israel would remain in Lebanon 'as long as necessary.'

key_facts.fact: The memorandum of understanding has been signed electronically by both sides; a formal signing ceremony is planned for Friday in Geneva, opening a 60-day window for technical negotiations on Iran's nuclear program.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials say negotiations over a final deal would take place in a 60-day window after the memorandum of understanding to end nearly four months of war triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran is physically signed.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Iran will receive half of its roughly $24 billion in long-frozen funds before final negotiations begin; a US official said Iran will get none of the money until it demonstrates compliance.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's powerful Revolutionary Guard said under the agreement, the country will receive half of its roughly $24 billion in long-frozen funds before final negotiations begin during a 60-day ceasefire extension. A U.S. official said earlier that Iran will get none of the money until it demonstrates compliance with the deal's terms.

key_facts.fact: Two regional officials told AP the interim deal would require Israel to leave nearly all the territory it occupies in Lebanon, minus a few hilltop points along the border; Iran insisted on adding Lebanon in the deal's last days.
key_facts.excerpt: The officials, speaking to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity to discuss the closed-door negotiations, said it would require Israel to leave nearly all the territory it occupies in Lebanon, minus a few hilltop points along the border seized earlier. The officials say Iran insisted the accord include Lebanon in the last days of the negotiations.

stories.headline: G7 Evian summit issues joint statement backing US-Iran deal, pledges Strait of Hormuz mine-clearing mission

key_facts.fact: G7 leaders meeting at Evian adopted joint statements on the US-Iran peace deal and on geopolitical issues, plus declarations on migrant smuggling, drug trafficking, partnerships and calls on Ebola response and cancer.
key_facts.excerpt: At the 2026 G7 Leaders' Summit held in Evian, the leaders of the G7 discussed topics ranging from international peace and security to global economic stability, growth, and emerging technologies. They adopted the following statements: Leaders' declaration on mutually beneficial international partnerships; Leaders' call for a coordinated response to the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak; Leaders' call on the fight against cancer; G7 Leaders' statement on geopolitical issues; Leaders' declaration on tackling migrant smugling; Leaders' declaration on the fight against drug trafficking.

key_facts.fact: UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada, Australia, EU and 9 other partners welcomed the MoU and committed to a 'strictly defensive and independent mission to reassure commercial shipping and conduct mine clearance operations' in the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: The urgent re-opening of the Strait of Hormuz with unconditional and unrestricted freedom of navigation is essential. We are committed to playing our part to achieve this — in accordance with our respective constitutional requirements — including through a strictly defensive and independent mission to reassure commercial shipping and conduct mine clearance operations.

key_facts.fact: The statement said Iran must never acquire a nuclear weapon and signatories are prepared to lift relevant sanctions in response to clear, verifiable steps by Iran on its nuclear program.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran must never acquire a nuclear weapon. We stand ready to work with the US, Iran and the IAEA to this end. We are prepared to lift relevant sanctions in response to clear, verifiable steps by Iran on its nuclear programme.

key_facts.fact: Trump told fellow leaders in Evian: 'There's an agreement about one thing, that Iran will never have a [nuclear weapon], never, ever, ever. The rest of it's irrelevant, frankly.'
key_facts.excerpt: In Evian, US President Donald Trump assured fellow leaders that Tehran would not have a nuclear weapon. 'There's an agreement about one thing, that Iran will never have a [nuclear weapon], never, ever, ever. The rest of it's irrelevant, frankly,' Mr Trump said.

key_facts.fact: Arab leaders from UAE, Qatar and Egypt attended Tuesday's session; the summit also addresses Ukraine, with European leaders pressing Trump to rethink his Ukraine strategy.
key_facts.excerpt: European leaders will warn U.S. President Donald Trump at Tuesday's G7 summit that a superficial interim Iran deal risks entrenching Tehran's nuclear and ballistic missile programmes, while also pressing him to rethink his Ukraine strategy.

stories.headline: Brent crude closes below $80 for first time since March on Hormuz reopening hopes

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures fell 5% to close at $78.96 per barrel on Tuesday, the first time the international benchmark has settled below $80 since March.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures fell 5% to close at $78.96 per barrel, the first time the international benchmark has fallen below $80 since March. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures lost 5.8% to settle at $76.05.

key_facts.fact: WTI crude has plunged nearly 20% since the beginning of June, underlining the Strait of Hormuz's importance.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. benchmark, West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude, fell 4% to $77.43 a barrel. WTI crude has plunged by nearly 20% since the beginning of June, underlining the Strait of Hormuz's continued importance to the oil market.

key_facts.fact: Trump said on arrival at G7 that the Strait of Hormuz will 'completely reopen' on Friday, free of Iranian tolls, after a signing ceremony in Geneva.
key_facts.excerpt: Arriving at the G7 meeting, President Donald Trump said the peace framework with Iran has been signed, adding that the Strait of Hormuz will 'completely reopen' on Friday, free of Iranian tolls. Trump said a formal signing ceremony would take place on Friday in Geneva.

key_facts.fact: BBC Verify's analysis of MarineTraffic data found just seven vessels appear to have passed through the strait since the deal was announced, while as many as 580 ships were waiting in the Gulf.
key_facts.excerpt: BBC Verify analysis of MarineTraffic ship-tracking data, however, shows that just seven vessels appear to have passed through the critical waterway since the deal was announced and as many as 580 ships appear to be waiting in the Gulf.

key_facts.fact: Mitsui OSK Lines CEO Jotaro Tamura said many tanker operators could wait weeks before allowing their tankers to resume transit through the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: Jotaro Tamura, chief executive of Mitsui OSK Lines, told the Financial Times on Tuesday that many operators could wait weeks until they allow their tankers to resume transit through the strait.

key_facts.excerpt: Senior Trump administration officials had weighed how to structure potential government equity stakes in major AI companies before the government's export controls on Anthropic further roiled the industry.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent favored using equity in AI firms to seed Trump Accounts, while Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick preferred directing equity to a sovereign wealth fund.

stories.headline: SpaceX briefly tops Microsoft, passes Amazon to become fifth most valuable company on day 3 of trading

key_facts.fact: SpaceX shares rose 4.83% to close at $201.80 on Tuesday, giving the company a market value of roughly $2.655 trillion — about $10 billion more than Amazon, until Tuesday the fifth-largest US-listed firm.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX shares rose 4.8% to close at $201.80, giving Elon Musk's company a market value of roughly $2.655 trillion -- some $800 billion more than its value when it sold its record initial public offering last week and about $10 billion more than that of Amazon, until Tuesday the fifth-largest U.S.-listed firm by market value.

key_facts.fact: Intraday, SpaceX's market value briefly topped Microsoft's $2.92 trillion before paring gains.
key_facts.excerpt: Tuesday saw SpaceX's stock climb as much as 15% in early trading, which pushed the company's market cap beyond the $2.66 trillion valuation for Amazon and Microsoft's $2.93 trillion market value. That briefly made it the fourth-largest global company by market cap before some of those gains were pared back.

key_facts.fact: More than 500,000 SpaceX options contracts changed hands within the first hour of trading and more than 1 million by early afternoon, in the debut session for SpaceX options.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 500,000 SpaceX options contracts changed hands within the first hour of trading and more than 1 million by early afternoon, according to Trade Alert data. SpaceX's heavily bullish options trading volume likely helped lift the stock early in the session, said Brent Kochuba, founder of options analytics service SpotGamma.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is set for fast-track inclusion in the Nasdaq 100, which would make it a major holding for passive index-tracking funds.
key_facts.excerpt: The rally could continue, analysts said, as SpaceX is set for fast-track inclusion in the Nasdaq 100, which will soon make it a major holding for passive funds and ETFs that track the index, creating a fresh source of demand for its shares.

key_facts.fact: Underwriters exercised the 'greenshoe' option, raising total IPO proceeds to $85.7 billion from $75 billion. SpaceX revenue was $18.7 billion in 2025, up 33% YoY, with a $4.9 billion loss.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's revenue jumped to $18.7 billion in 2025, 33% higher than the previous year, a financial filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission showed. Nearly a quarter of that revenue came from Starlink, which counted millions of subscribers. Still, SpaceX failed to turn a profit, registering a loss of $4.9 billion last year.

stories.headline: Binance set to lose EU access as Greek regulator poised to reject MiCA license bid

key_facts.fact: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, is set to lose permission to offer services to EU clients within weeks as its license application is about to be rejected, sources told Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, is set to lose permission to serve European Union clients from next month because its licence application is about to be rejected, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: Under MiCA rules, crypto firms have until the end of June 2026 to obtain a license; without it, Binance would not qualify to operate in the EU from July 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Under new EU rules, called MiCA, crypto firms have until the end of June to obtain a licence to allow them to keep servicing clients across the bloc. Binance's application, made to Greece's market regulator, is set to be turned down, the people said.

key_facts.fact: Binance has 300 million customers worldwide and has pursued the MiCA license for 18 months; the application was made through Greece's Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC).
key_facts.excerpt: A spokesperson for Binance, which has 300 million customers worldwide, earlier said it has been pursuing a MiCA licence and had worked with regulators for 18 months.

key_facts.fact: Binance disputed the report, saying its understanding is that the HCMC considered its application compliant with MiCA requirements.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Our understanding is that the HCMC completed its review of the application and considered it compliant with MiCA requirements, and that the application was also reviewed at ESMA level,' a Binance spokesman told CoinDesk via email.

key_facts.fact: Co-CEO Richard Teng had said in February that Greece's labour force and security profile gave it the edge over larger financial centres as Binance's regulatory home in Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said in February that Greece's labour force and security profile gave it the edge over larger financial centres for its regulatory home in Europe.
